source.title: Polylogarithmic width suffices for gradient descent to achieve arbitrarily small test error with shallow ReLU networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper is a theoretical analysis of shallow ReLU networks, but it does not report whether they fit random labels or any of the other behaviors named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses how random labels reduce the infinite-width NTK separation margin and gives a theoretical initialization-separability result for noisy 2-XOR data. Neither result measures training error after fitting random labels.
record.test_reason: Theorem 2.2, combined with Section 5's positive-margin guarantee for arbitrary labels on nonparallel inputs, proves that sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks trained by gradient descent attain arbitrarily small training loss, including for random labels. This bears on V1 through a theoretical method, although neither extracted row captures that training result.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes two subsidiary separability results but omits the central conclusion: gradient descent and online SGD on sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks have optimization and generalization guarantees controlled by an NTK separation margin. Width is polylogarithmic in sample size and inverse target error when margin dependence is held fixed; random labels can make the margin small. The training guarantee applies to arbitrary labels on nonparallel inputs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives theoretical guarantees for two-layer ReLU networks trained on data satisfying a positive separation assumption; it does not reproduce the cited random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The separation margin depends on the label assignment; the initialization-separability result depends on width and the noisy 2-XOR setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 5.2 states that random labeling gives an infinite-width NTK margin at most 1/√(20n) with probability 0.9, although the proof does not justify that constant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random labels yield a small infinite-width NTK separation margin; this alone establishes neither fitting performance nor training-time ratios.

fits_no_version.finding: For the specified four-point noisy 2-XOR subset, initialized features can be nonseparable with probability at least one half when m ≤ √(d−2)/4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow networks can lack initial feature separability on this structured dataset; this does not establish failure after training.

record.problems: The random-label result is a theoretical bound on an infinite-width kernel margin, not an observed network training outcome. The narrow-width result is specific to a four-point noisy 2-XOR subset and concerns separability at initialization.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error under random labeling; empirical performance of standard deep architectures; fitting random labels using the same architecture and hyperparameters as a true-label comparison. The sufficient width depends on the separation margin.

Actual or tightly characterized training-time ratios for true versus random labels, and convergence across increasing corruption fractions. Margin-dependent upper bounds do not establish these comparisons.
Training outcomes on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Comparisons involving weight decay, dropout, or augmentation, including their removal and true-label generalization.
The temporal ordering of learning shared patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

missing.what: Theoretical random-label fitting guarantee: Theorem 2.2 gives average empirical logistic loss ≤ ε within T = ⌈2λ²/(ηε)⌉ iterations, with probability at least 1−3δ, for m ≥ 4096λ²/γ⁶ and constant positive η ≤ 1. Section 5 establishes positive γ for arbitrary binary labels when inputs are nonparallel. Record this combined implication, with its width and input assumptions.
missing.locator: Section 2, Theorem 2.2; Section 5, Proposition 5.1 and the arbitrary-label lower bound immediately preceding Proposition 5.2.

record.verdict_notes: The results are theoretical, not empirical. Proposition 5.2's proof gives an expected quadratic form of 1/(2n); Markov's inequality yields a 0.9-probability upper bound of 5/n, not 1/(20n). Its qualitative O(n^−1/2) margin conclusion survives this constant correction.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks fit completely random labels to near-zero training error and have test error at chance without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time for random versus true labels and how convergence changes as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep from clean to fully randomized labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels during training.

rows.subject: infinite-width NTK K1
rows.operation_detail: Bounds the separation margin after replacing true labels with random labels.
rows.uncertainty: with probability 0.9 over the random labels
rows.note: This is a theoretical margin bound, not a measurement of network training or test error.
rows.check: The stated margin bound matches Proposition 5.2, but margin alone does not measure random-label fitting or comparative training time. The proposition's numerical constant is also inconsistent with its proof's expectation and Markov argument.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU network at initialization
rows.operation_detail: Analyzes whether the initialized training features are separable on a four-point subset of noisy 2-XOR data.

conditions.value: arbitrary subset of four noisy 2-XOR points with the same last (d − 2) coordinates

rows.measure: Existence of a weight matrix V separating all four initialized feature vectors
rows.value: With probability 1/2 over initialization, no such V exists.
rows.note: This concerns initial feature separability on noisy 2-XOR data, not random-label fitting.
rows.check: This is a theoretical result about separability of initialized features, not trained-network error. Noisy 2-XOR has deterministic labels and irrelevant input coordinates; it is not randomly corrupted labeling.

relationships.condition: Theoretical fitting guarantee for sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks on a finite training set with nonparallel normalized inputs and arbitrary binary labels.
relationships.reason: Based on text missing from the rows: Theorem 2.2 guarantees arbitrarily small empirical logistic loss under gradient descent; Section 5 establishes its separability assumption for arbitrary labels, including random labels. Small logistic loss entails small training classification error.
relationships.display_finding: Gradient descent achieves arbitrarily small empirical logistic loss for arbitrary labels, including random labels, implying small training classification error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
